Questo documento spiega, passo per passo: This document explains, step by step, how the program derives the efficiency of a meteor shower for a meteor scatter path. Each step states where it comes from: a published source, a check made on the program, or a choice made by the program itself. The complete, numbered equations are in the Manual of calculations (doc folder).
il passo riprende una fonte citata; il n: the step follows a cited source; the number in square brackets refers to the list of sources at the end.
confronto tra il programma e le fonti, c: comparison between the program and the sources, with the result of the check.
scelta del programma, non presa da una f: choice made by the program, not taken from a source: to be verified by on-air experience.
L'efficienza indica in percentuale quant: The efficiency indicates as a percentage how much the position of the shower allows reflections on a given path. The concept is due to Ilkka OH5IY (MS-Soft) [2] and is taken up in the article [1]: the efficiency maximum does not coincide with the visual maximum (ZHR), because it depends on where the radiant lies relative to the two stations.
MCG_MS di DL5MCG [3] applica lo stesso c: DL5MCG's MCG_MS [3] applies the same concept to four fixed directions (N/S, NE/SW, E/W, SE/NW) and, when the DX station's locator is entered, also to the real path.
YA-MS calcola l'efficienza per la tratta: YA-MS calculates the efficiency for the real path between the two locators, not for fixed directions.
2. Dove avvengono le riflessioni: lo str: 2. Where reflections take place: the E layer
Le meteore dello sciame producono scie i: The meteors of the shower produce ionised trails in the E layer, between 80 and 120 km in height. The SKiYMET radars give a mean height of about 90 km [1].
Il programma legge l'istogramma delle qu: The program reads the height histogram of the Collm radar [7] and uses the most frequent height (the mode) as the calculation height. If the "from radar" checkbox is unticked, the value entered by hand is used.
Grafico di Collm del 5/11/2026: moda 89,: Collm plot of 5/11/2026: mode 89.5 km, mean 88.6 km, standard deviation 6.8 km. The figure confirms the 90 km of the article [1].
DJ5HG [18] e QTFGUI [17] usano una quota: DJ5HG [18] and QTFGUI [17] use a fixed height of 102 km; the program prefers the value measured by the radar. Recommendation ITU-R P.843 [24] gives a mean height h = 124 − 17·log10(f) km: about 97 km at 36.2 MHz and 87 km at 144 MHz, in line with the Collm mode (89.5 km on 5/11/2026).
Terra sferica di raggio r = 6372,7955 km: Spherical Earth of radius r = 6372.7955 km [1].
La tratta è sempre quella reale tra il l: The path is always the real one between the station's locator and that of the DX station. Distance, azimuth and midpoint are calculated with the great-circle formulas.
I calcoli che dipendono dall'ora si rife: Time-dependent calculations refer to the midpoint of the path: the best time can differ by up to 1.5 hours between the two ends (SM6FHZ [4]).

Con H = 89,5 km e il lobo a 0° la portat: With H = 89.5 km and the lobe at 0° the range is 1062 km. If the path is longer than twice the range, the two stations do not see a common zone of the E layer.
Questi due punti sono i bordi più lontan: These two points are the farthest edges of the sky seen by both stations, not the points where most reflections arrive. On the path JN70CN - IN78UO (1710 km) they lie 37° to the left and right of the direct direction, whereas MSHV recommends 10°. This is why the program calls them "Limit A" and "Limit B" and draws them faintly on the map, with the two circles of the common zone.
Nell'esempio dell'articolo (JN44BB - IO5: In the example of the article (JN44BB - IO53RT) the drawing places these intersections about 870 km from the stations: this corresponds to a lobe elevated by about 2° (865 km).
3.4 Hot A e Hot B: dove puntare: 3.4 Hot A and Hot B: where to point
Le riflessioni delle meteore sporadiche: Reflections from sporadic meteors concentrate in two zones ("hot spots") on either side of the path midpoint. J. Richardson (AMS) [19], in the table quoted by DJ5HG [18], gives the antenna offset from the direct direction: 13° at 1000 km, 11° at 1250 km, 10° at 1500 and at 2000 km. AMS Bulletin No. 203, quoted by W8WN [14], gives 10° at 1500 and 1800 km.
Hot A e Hot B sono i punti a distanza s: Hot A and Hot B are the points at distance s from the midpoint, perpendicular to the path (A on the left looking from the station towards the DX station, B on the right). With the "auto (AMS)" checkbox ticked (the default) s comes from the offset in Richardson's table, linearly interpolated (13° below 1000 km, 10° above 2000 km): s = (D/2)·tan(offset). Unticking the checkbox lets you enter s by hand (MSHV [15] uses 150 km).
Con la tabella AMS: 1000 km → 13°, s ≈ 1: With the AMS table: 1000 km → 13°, s ≈ 115 km; 1250 km → 11°, s ≈ 121 km; 1500 km → 10°, s ≈ 132 km; 2000 km → 10°, s ≈ 176 km. JN70CN-IN78UO (1710 km) → 10°, s ≈ 151 km, like the 150 km used previously and by MSHV; on short paths the table brings the hot spots closer to the midpoint.
Per l'ora mostrata sulla volta celeste i: For the time shown on the Sky view the program sums, over all showers above the horizon, ZHR x efficiency split between side A and side B (chapter 7.1). The hot spot on the side receiving more reflections is the recommended one: it appears in red on the map.

DF5HC also gives the best distance as 1300-1500 km, with a maximum slightly beyond 2000 km.

Ascensione retta, declinazione, longitud: Right ascension, declination, solar longitude of the maximum, velocity, r index and ZHR come from the IMO 2026 and 2027 calendars [5], tables 5 and 7; the Antihelion source from table 6. The minor showers of the IMO list are also included, for example the October Camelopardalids (OCT, ZHR 5, active on 5-6 October), the Andromedids and the daytime radio showers of April and May: even with small ZHRs they contribute to the path index and to the hot spot recommendation.
Per gli sciami diurni radio l'IMO non dà: For the daytime radio showers the IMO gives neither ZHR nor velocity: the program uses a working value of 5.
Longitudine solare (equinozio J2000), te: Solar longitude (equinox J2000), sidereal time and conversion to azimuth and elevation: formulas of Meeus [6].
La deriva giornaliera del radiante usa v: The daily radiant drift uses working values, written in the file sciami.csv and editable.
Il programma mostra sempre il prossimo m: The program always shows the next maximum. When the IMO has published the calendar for that year (2026 and 2027 are already included in massimi_imo.csv) it uses the IMO date and time [5]; otherwise it calculates the instant at which the Sun reaches the longitude of the maximum.
Il calcolo coincide con i calendari IMO: The calculation agrees with the IMO 2026 and 2027 calendars within a few minutes for the showers for which the IMO gives the time (for example Quadrantids 3/1/2026 21:13 versus 21:00, Geminids 14/12/2027 19:51 versus 20:00). The exceptions are the daytime kappa-Leonids 2026, one day later (26/9 instead of 25/9), and the time of the eta-Aquariids 2027 (15:10 versus the IMO's 09:00): in these cases the IMO value applies.

Una scia rimanda il segnale tra le due s: A trail sends the signal between the two stations only if it is tangent to an ellipsoid with the stations at its foci (McKinley [8]). The trails of a shower are parallel to the radiant direction [1, 8].
In pratica, per ogni punto P dello strat: In practice, for each point P of the E layer the directions from P towards the two stations and their bisector n are taken. The trail, parallel to the radiant (direction s), reflects towards both stations when it is perpendicular to the bisector:
La stessa legge è alla base di QTFGUI di: The same law underlies DJ5HG's QTFGUI: the ray that hits the trail is scattered on a cone around it, and only those on the cone receive the signal. The cone condition is equivalent to s · n = 0. [17, 18] In his 2004 text DJ5HG describes it like this: the trail crosses the E layer, the two antennas illuminate it and the receiver lies on the cone that has the trail as its axis; the wall of the cone is the lobe of a radiator thousands of wavelengths long, hence narrow, but at grazing incidence (long paths) it touches the ground over a wide area.
La condizione si accetta con una tollera: The condition is accepted with a Gaussian tolerance of 0.05 rad (about 3°). For an ideal trail the wall of the cone is much narrower [18]; the 3° represent what the ideal cone does not see: the spread of the radiants of a shower (0.3-1.4° measured by the GMN), the trail bent by the wind and its finite length.
Per il meteor scatter QTFGUI di DJ5HG di: For meteor scatter DJ5HG's QTFGUI draws deviations from the reflection law of up to 32°: the program's Gaussian tolerance of 0.05 rad is stricter and concentrates the weight on almost exactly specular points. With 5 km sampling instead of 15 km the percentages change by less than 0.3 points.
Una scia rimanda il segnale tra le due s: A trail sends the signal between the two stations only if it is tangent to an ellipsoid with the stations at its foci: at each point of the E layer only the radiants on the semicircle of the sky perpendicular to the bisector of the scattering angle are useful (Eshleman and Mlodnosky [20]; Meeks and James [21]). Near the midpoint this semicircle rises highest across the path: a radiant at elevation El produces specular trails about H·tan El to the side of the midpoint, on the side opposite the radiant, i.e. in the hot spots that Eshleman and Mlodnosky and Recommendation ITU-R P.843 [24] place about 100 km on either side. The number of trails and their ionisation increase with sin El [21]. The dependence of the echoes on the radiant position was calculated by Hines [22] and verified on four showers by Forsyth, Hines and Vogan [23]. From this follows the practical rule of SM6FHZ [4]: best path orthogonal to the radiant azimuth, pointing Az ± 90°, tolerance ±40-50°.
Riserva di DJ5HG [18]: con il radiante b: Reservation by DJ5HG [18]: with a low radiant lying right along the path McKinley's formula gives strong signals, even though the meteors are few (Hamburg-Narvik, Quadrantids, around 19 UTC). The rule "radiant aligned with the path = almost zero efficiency" therefore holds for a high radiant, not for a grazing one. The program stays cautious and does not raise the efficiency, but shows "LOW RADIANT ALONG THE PATH" on the Sky view when an active shower has its radiant below 20° and within 30° of the path direction. The gap with the radiant at the zenith between the two stations is confirmed (Quadrantids, Hamburg-Barcelona, around 08 UTC).
La stessa regola compare nella formula d: The same rule appears in the formula of DH9GCD quoted by DF5HC [16]: effectiveness = sin(El) · cos(El) · sin(P − Az), with El and Az the elevation and azimuth of the radiant and P the azimuth of the DX station. It is maximum with the radiant at 45° and across the path; DF5HC considers the radiant too low below 20° and too high above 70°. The formula takes no account of distance or heights, but it is a good term of comparison: in the sub-tab "Forecast calculation › Efficiency calculation" it appears in light blue under each shower, as a percentage of its maximum (0.5). When the radiant is above 70° as seen from the station the program flags it with ↑ in the table and with a warning on the Sky view.
La formula di DH9GCD non ha una fonte pr: The DH9GCD formula has no published primary source: it combines the factor sin El (number and ionisation of the trails) with a factor cos El that represents how far the specular point moves away from the centre of the path as the radiant rises. Calculated with the radiant seen from the midpoint, as MS-Soft [25] does, it reproduces the MS-Soft table for KP30HV-JO52MM (1324 km, Quadrantids, 4/1/2001) within 4 points between 16° and 48° of elevation and within 16 points up to 64°, with the same maximum at 13 UT (96 % versus 92 %). It remains a term of comparison.
6. Dal singolo punto all'efficienza: 6. From the single point to the efficiency
Il programma divide lo strato E in punti: The program divides the E layer into points every 15 km and keeps only those that both stations see above the minimum elevation of the lobe.
La potenza di una scia sottodensa (McKin: The power of an underdense trail (McKinley [8]; ITU-R P.843 [24]) increases with λ³ and decreases with the distances R1, R2 from the stations; φ is half the scattering angle, β the angle between the trail and the plane containing the two stations and the point:
peso = 1 / [ R1 · R2 · (R1 + R2) · (1 −: weight = 1 / [ R1 · R2 · (R1 + R2) · (1 − cos²β · sin²φ) ]
Fino alla versione 1.6 il programma pren: Up to version 1.6 the program took β = 0 for all trails (weight with cos²φ): trails crossing the plane of the path weighed up to 10-15 dB too much. From 1.7 β can be calculated for each point and each radiant direction with the option "Angle β between trail and path (full McKinley)", on by default because it gives the most cautious values (no trail is overestimated).
L'angolo φ è limitato a 85° per evitare: The angle φ is limited to 85° to avoid infinite values in grazing directions.
Il numero di meteore che arrivano in un: The number of meteors arriving at a point is proportional to the sine of the radiant elevation at that point: it is the same correction with which the IMO calculates the ZHR [5].
Opzione \"Scie più lunghe con il radiant: Option "Longer trails with a low radiant (DJ5HG)", off by default, in Efficiency calculation: DJ5HG [18] observes that with a low radiant fewer meteors fall per km² but the trails are longer (up to 100 km usable) and satisfy the reflection law more often. With the option on the weight becomes min(sin El, 15/100): the usable thickness of the layer, 15 km, divided by the sine of the elevation gives the trail length, limited to 100 km. Above about 9° of elevation the two effects cancel out; with the option off, the calculation stays cautious.
Impostazioni pronte del calcolo, nella s: Calculation presets, on the same row: "Cautious" (the default, the most cautious values: height from the radar, normal trails, with β), "As DJ5HG" (102 km, long trails, with β) and "Custom", which is selected automatically when the height, the "from radar" checkbox, the long trails or the angle β are changed by hand.
Effetto dell'angolo β sulla direzione mi: Effect of the angle β on the best direction, 1000 km path: without β the maximum lies between 15° and 90° from the path depending on the radiant elevation (30° with the radiant at 30°, perpendicular with the radiant at 60°) and the perpendicular radiant is worth 67 % with the radiant at 30°; with β the maximum is always with the radiant along the path and the perpendicular radiant drops to 15 %. With β the best-direction rule of SM6FHZ and DH9GCD is therefore lost: this is why β is an option, on by default because it gives the most cautious values (no trail is overestimated).
Per ogni direzione del radiante si somma: For each radiant direction the weights of all points where the trail reflects are summed. 100% is the most favourable radiant position for that path:
Accanto alla percentuale, che vale per q: Next to the percentage, which applies to that path only, the program gives the efficiency in dB relative to the fixed reference of DJ5HG [18]: 0 dB is the maximum of a 1000 km north-south path straddling the equator with the radiant on the celestial equator at the equinox (the radiant rises in the east, passes through the zenith and sets in the west), calculated with the same height and the same weights. In this way different paths can be compared with each other. DJ5HG states an accuracy better than 6 dB for his values.

La documentazione di MS-Soft 5.2 [25] de: The MS-Soft 5.2 documentation [25] defines OH5IY's efficiency as a relative index for underdense trails only, with two factors: radiant elevation (optimum about 45°) and angle with the path (90° = maximum). The minimum is raised by hand to 20 % for overdense trails; the formula is not published. MCG_MS [3] calculates the efficiency for four fixed directions and, when the DX station's locator is entered, also for the real path.
Per ogni ora il programma calcola quale: For each hour the program calculates which part of the reflections falls to the left of the path (side A) and which to the right (side B). The hourly table shows the letter of the prevailing side.
Conviene spostare il puntamento di 10-30: It is worth shifting the pointing by 10-30° towards that side (side-scatter) [1].
L'indice riassume in un numero quanto il: The index sums up in one number how much the showers as a whole favour the path in a given hour:
I = Σ ZHR · η / 100 (su tutti gli sci: I = Σ  ZHR · η / 100   (over all active showers)
Sulla volta celeste il pallino del radia: On the Sky view the radiant dot is yellow with efficiency ≥ 50% and ZHR ≥ 2, orange with efficiency ≥ 20%, dark red below 20%, grey when the shower is almost inactive.
Per l'ora mostrata il programma somma, p: For the time shown the program sums, point by point of the E layer, the contribution of each active shower to the efficiency (the same specular reflection condition as in chapter 5), weighted by the ZHR. The points with at least 3 % of the maximum form the PREV zones, one per side of the path, drawn in plan view as ellipses: centre = weighted mean of the points, axes = twice their spread. This is the practical rule: if the shower moves from north to south, the useful trails fall to the east and west. The yellow line shows the direction of motion (radiant azimuth) of the selected shower, or of the most favourable one.
La sezione mostra le stesse scie viste d: The section shows the same trails seen from the station with the antenna pointed towards the DX station: horizontally the azimuth relative to the DX station (A on the left, B on the right), vertically the elevation. For each shower the 14 strongest reflection points are taken; each trail is a segment oriented towards the radiant, from 10 km above to 10 km below the trail height (at most 60 km per side), thicker the more probable it is. Also drawn are the antenna lobe (−3 dB circle around the lobe elevation), the DX station and Hot A / Hot B.
Regole sperimentali di SM6FHZ [4]: il nu: Experimental rules of SM6FHZ [4]: the number and intensity of reflections scale with λ³, the duration with λ². In forward scatter the duration also increases with sec²φ (τ = λ²·sec²φ / 16π²D, McKinley [8]; OH5IY [25]): the Collm radar measures in backscatter (φ = 0), so on the path the duration must be multiplied by sec²φ at the midpoint (×4 at 60°, ×8.5 at 70°, ×33 at 80°).
In McKinley [8] λ³ è la potenza di una s: In McKinley [8] λ³ is the power of a single underdense trail, not the number of trails. At a fixed threshold and with mass index s, the number of trails above the threshold scales with λ raised to 1.5·(s − 1), i.e. about λ^1.5 for s = 2 (IZ5TEK [26]; OH5IY [25]). The program keeps k = 3, the experimental rule of SM6FHZ [4], and says so: with k = 3, 1000 meteors/hour at Collm become about 16 reflections/hour at 144 MHz, with k = 1.5 about 127. RMOB observers of the GRAVES radar at 143.050 MHz [13] typically count 20 to 140 echoes/hour; the right value of k for one's own station is obtained from the comparison with RMOB (next section).
Durata massima di un ping secondo IARU R: Maximum ping duration according to IARU Region 1: 1000 ms at 50 MHz, 500 ms at 70 MHz, 100 ms at 144 MHz, 13 ms at 432 MHz [1].

Riferimenti: 172–190 dB dai calcoli di G: References: 172–190 dB from G4BAO's calculations, quoted by GM8JBJ (from Kaiser & Closs [9]); about 200 dB on average at 144 MHz (OH5IY); minimum receivable signal −130 dBm [1].
Con q = 10¹⁴ elettroni/m, scie a 89,5 km: With q = 10¹⁴ electrons/m, trails at 89.5 km and β = 0, at 144 MHz the result is 182–192 dB between 600 and 2100 km (185 dB at 1000 km). The range of 172–190 dB calculated by John Worsnop G4BAO in his doctoral thesis, quoted by GM8JBJ [9], includes these values. With β = 90° the loss increases by 10 dB at 600 km, 13 dB at 1000 km and 16 dB at 2100 km: OH5IY's average of 200 dB cited in the article [1] lies between the two cases. Again according to GM8JBJ, G4BAO finds about 6 dB less for trails aligned with the path.
I 182 dB della tabella di GM8JBJ [9] non: The 182 dB of GM8JBJ's table [9] are not a confirmation: the table does not state the frequency, its 86.4 dB per leg are the free-space loss over 500 km at 1 MHz (the 20 log f term is missing: at 144 MHz it is 129.6 dB) and the sum of the entries, 86.4 + 0 − 9 + 86.4, is 163.8 dB and not 182. The page mentions neither a minimum value nor 144 MHz.
Raggio iniziale alla quota media degli e: Initial radius at the mean echo height, h = 124 − 17 log f [24]: r0 = 0.76 m at 95 km for 50 MHz, 0.40 m at 87 km for 144 MHz, 0.21 m at 79 km for 432 MHz. Over 1000 km a1 is 0.2 dB at 50 MHz, 0.6 dB at 144 MHz and 1.4 dB at 432 MHz (2.9 dB at 600 km). At DJ5HG's fixed height of 102 km it would give about 70 dB at 432 MHz, i.e. no echo: this is why the mean echo height at the frequency is used.
Il modello considera solo le scie sottod: The model considers only underdense trails. Overdense trails (the long bursts) and the sporadic background do not enter the efficiency; the sporadic background is represented by the radar flux.
Nel calcolo dell'efficienza le antenne s: In the efficiency calculation the antennas are considered isotropic; the real lobe is used only for the Hot check.
Le derive del radiante e i coefficienti: The radiant drifts and the B coefficients of the activity profile are working values.
Le percentuali vanno confrontate con MCG: The percentages should be compared with MCG_MS, MS-Soft and with on-air observations.

Misure reali (HamSCI, Meteor Scatter QSO: Real measurements (HamSCI, Meteor Scatter QSO Party [29]): R. Suggs NN4NT measured the power decay constant of 1298 underdense echoes in the MSK144 recordings of NN4SA (EM64) during the 2026 Perseids (4736 WSJT-X WAV files). Medians: 148 ms at 28.145 MHz (41 echoes), 78 ms at 50.260 MHz (1198), 53 ms at 144.150 MHz (59). With λ² starting from 6 m they would be about 245 ms and 9.5 ms: on 2 m pings last more than five times longer than predicted. The author attributes this to a probable echo ceiling height effect on 2 m: at high frequencies mainly the low trails remain visible, where diffusion is slower. It is a preliminary analysis: a single receiving station, different distances not normalised with sec²φ, only echoes strong enough to be detected.
Weitzen e Ralston [27]: la costante di d: Weitzen and Ralston [27]: the decay constant varies from trail to trail with an exponential distribution, with mean τ = λ²·sec²φ / (32π²D) (power constant; 16π² applies to the amplitude). Xia, Li and Zheng [28] give D as a function of height, D = 10^(0.067·h − 5.6) m²/s: over 1000 km with the trail at 95 km this gives τ ≈ 47 ms at 144 MHz and 390 ms at 50 MHz. The 144 MHz value is close to the measured median, the 50 MHz one is five times higher: D grows tenfold every 15 km of height, so the height of the visible trails, which changes with frequency, weighs on the duration more than λ².
Il programma offre la scelta \"Durata de: The program offers the choice "Ping duration between bands" in the Geometry and path loss sub-tab. Theoretical (default, cautious): λ², which gives the shortest pings. Observed: linear interpolation on a logarithmic scale between the three NN4SA medians; below 28 MHz the 10–6 m segment is extended, above 144 MHz, where there are no measurements, λ² is used again. With the observed choice a 1 s echo at Collm (36.2 MHz) lasts about 473 ms at 144 MHz instead of 63 ms, and from 50 to 144 MHz pings become 1.5 times shorter instead of 8.
Incertezza del raggio iniziale: Stober e: Uncertainty of the initial radius: Stober et al. [30], with the CMOR radar at 17.45, 29.85 and 38.15 MHz and a full wave scattering model, find between 85 and 95 km r0 of 0.5–2 m, mostly 1–1.5 m, with a scatter of a factor of two at each height; for transverse polarisation the values are about twice the earlier measurements (Greenhow and Hall 1960; Jones and Campbell-Brown 2005). Only about 5 % of echoes can be described by the ideal model. The ITU-R P.843 formula [24] gives 0.5 m at 90 km and 0.75 m at 95 km, i.e. the lower limit of these measurements.
Il programma offre la scelta \"Raggio in: The program offers the choice "Initial trail radius" in the Geometry and path loss sub-tab: twice the ITU value (default, cautious, like the measurements of Stober et al.), ITU-R P.843, excluded. Doubling r0 multiplies the factor a1 in dB by 4: over 1000 km 0.8 dB at 50 MHz, 2.4 dB at 144 MHz and 5.6 dB at 432 MHz (11.6 dB at 600 km). The CMOR measurements are at lower frequencies and at 85–95 km: using them at 432 MHz, where echoes come from about 79 km, is an extrapolation.
